units.title: Inflammation is a response
units.lesson: Inflammation is part of the body’s response to tissue injury or threat. Innate immune mechanisms act rapidly and help recruit further responses. Infection involves a pathogen; inflammation can also occur after non-infectious injury. The concepts overlap but are not synonyms. A single inflammatory feature does not by itself identify a microorganism.
units.question: Which distinction is sound?
choices: Every inflammation proves a specific infection
units.explanation: Inflammation is a host response and can follow non-infectious injury.

units.title: Plug and reinforce
units.lesson: Following vascular injury, platelets help form an initial plug. Coagulation generates fibrin that reinforces clot formation. These mechanisms interact to limit blood loss. Describing the mechanisms is different from diagnosing a disorder or selecting a drug. In a theory answer, distinguish the cellular contribution from the coagulation-protein contribution.
units.question: Which contribution is cellular?
units.explanation: Platelets supply the cellular plug contribution.
rationales: This is the cellular haemostatic role.

units.title: Move air before discussing exchange
units.lesson: Pulmonary ventilation is movement of air into and out of the lungs. Pressure differences drive airflow. This is not identical to blood flow through lung vessels or to all the steps of oxygen delivery to tissues. Using precise terms prevents a revision answer from treating breathing movement and circulation as interchangeable measurements.
units.question: What is pulmonary ventilation?
choices: Movement of air into and out of the lungs
Only the flow of blood in arteries

units.title: Pressure is not flow
units.lesson: Blood flow is volume moving per unit time. Blood pressure is the force driving movement, and resistance opposes flow. These quantities are related but have different meanings and units. A pressure reading is not itself a flow measurement. This chapter introduces the relationship without establishing patient-specific thresholds or treatment decisions.
units.question: Which quantity is expressed as volume per unit time?
units.explanation: Flow describes movement of a volume over time.
rationales: Resistance relates pressure gradient and flow but is not itself volume per time.

units.question: A paper example describes inflammation after a sterile tissue injury. Which interpretation is sound?
choices: A host response can occur without infection

units.explanation: Inflammation is a response; infection is one possible cause.
rationales: A pathogen is not established by the response alone.

units.question: Which relationship is correct at a conceptual level?
choices: Pressure differences drive flow while resistance opposes it
Pressure and volume flow have identical units
Resistance is simply another name for blood volume per minute
units.explanation: Pressure, flow and resistance are related but different quantities.
rationales: This distinguishes driving force and opposition.
Pressure and flow use different units.
